metadata.name: litellm-oct-2026
metadata.title: LiteLLM 1.107.0 Compromise (Oct 2026)
metadata.description: Gh tokens stolen from BerriAI's internal LLM gateway logs redirect the release pipeline to a lookalike repo; poisoned PyPI/Docker

data.name: Abuse Local AI Tools
data.description: Attacker uses AI coding assistants to exfiltrate code or inject malicious suggestions
risks: Sensitive code sent to AI services

protective.name: Acceptable use policy against unapproved AI tools
Approved AI tools with data protection

detective.name: Network monitoring for AI service connections

data.customLabel: Contributing: Claude Code traffic carries developers' gh OAuth tokens
data.evidence: Not an attacker action. Coding-agent tool output (e.g. gh auth token, hosts.yml) travels in request/response bodies through the internal LiteLLM gateway, which logged full bodies [Maintainer + Inference]

data.name: Steal Secrets from Production Environment
data.description: Attacker accesses production secrets store and exfiltrates customer secrets, tokens, and credentials
risks: Encryption keys accessible in process memory
Lack of hardware security module (HSM) for key storage
Centralized storage of all customer secrets
No data loss prevention (DLP) on production systems

protective.name: Store encryption keys in HSM (Hardware Security Module)

data.customLabel: 3 gho_ tokens harvested from gateway logs via rogue 'innocuously named' user
data.evidence: Attacker accessed BerriAI's internal LiteLLM deployment and read logged request/response bodies containing three developers' GitHub CLI OAuth tokens; one belonged to one of two org owners, one could run workflows [Maintainer]

data.name: Abuse Credentials for VCS Access
data.description: Attacker uses stolen credentials to access VCS
risks: Credentials in public repos of org members
data.customLabel: Org-owner gh token used against private release repo
data.evidence: Stolen gho_ tokens are long-lived, not device-bound and carry the user's full rights, including org owner [Maintainer]

data.name: Malicious Code Modification in Repository
data.description: Attacker with repository access directly modifies source code to inject backdoors, malicious logic, or vulnerabilities into the codebase
risks: Direct push to protected branches allowed
No detection of suspicious code patterns

protective.name: Mandatory code review by multiple reviewers
Minimal VCS permissions (principle of least privilege)

data.customLabel: Branch protection disabled; source-repo override force-pushed (9cf97e9, 10:08:34Z)
data.evidence: Merge of 'releaser points at a different source repository' blocked by branch protection at 10:08:29Z; 5s later owner token disabled protection and force-pushed commit 9cf97e935aeaf791b9c8db224a2bb3ee156134ce [LiteLLM post-mortem]

data.name: Abuse Credentials for CI/CD Access
data.description: Attacker uses stolen credentials to access CI/CD system
data.customLabel: Staging run 11:08Z; 2nd stolen account approves prod environment 11:11Z
data.evidence: Release triggered with stolen credentials; production environment approval satisfied by a second compromised account at 11:11:18Z. Monday 10-19 temporary widening of release permissions broadened who could trigger/approve [LiteLLM post-mortem + Maintainer]

data.name: Malicious Execution in Workflow Context
data.description: Attacker executes malicious code within CI/CD workflow
risks: Using untrusted SW packages on runners
Using untrusted container / VM image for runners

protective.name: Automated maintainer reputation and hygiene checks

data.customLabel: Legitimate release build checks out Berri-AI/litellm (~11:21Z)
data.evidence: Identical build fingerprint to clean 1.106.2 (maturin 1.9.4, rustc 1.98.0, manylinux_2_28); payload in maturin .data/purelib layout, built in not repacked. Only dirty version among 42 since 10-01 [Verified]

data.name: Publishing Malicious Package
data.description: Attacker publishes malicious package to registry
data.customLabel: litellm==1.107.0 (7 wheels + sdist) via Trusted Publishing, 11:39Z
data.evidence: 8 files uploaded 11:39:51-11:40:13Z; live on PyPI until 13:23Z. Trusted Publishing held: it authenticated the workflow, not its input. No PEP 740 attestations [Verified + LiteLLM post-mortem]

data.name: Publishing Malicious Container/VM Image
data.description: Attacker publishes malicious container or VM image
data.customLabel: Docker v1.107.0, latest, main-latest, main-stable (COPY cook ./cook)
data.evidence: Final fork commit 20535d8f added COPY cook ./cook to backend/, gateway/, migrations/ Dockerfiles. Images signed and pushed 11:46:56Z; GHCR down by 13:51Z, Docker Hub 14:20Z. Index sha256:1bbcb144... [Verified + LiteLLM post-mortem]

data.name: Package Lifecycle Script Abuse
data.description: Attacker leverages package manager lifecycle hooks (postinstall, preinstall) or language-specific initialization mechanisms (.pth files) to execute malicious code during package installation
risks: Lifecycle scripts enabled by default in package managers
No review or approval of install-time scripts
Scripts execute with user privileges automatically
Python .pth files execute on any interpreter startup
No network restrictions during package installation

protective.name: Network isolation during package installation
protective.description: Block outbound network access during install phase to prevent payload download

protective.name: Lockfile integrity verification
protective.description: Use npm ci instead of npm install to enforce lockfile integrity

protective.name: Package version pinning with hash verification
protective.description: Pin exact versions with integrity hashes to prevent substitution

protective.name: Python .pth file restrictions
protective.description: Audit and restrict .pth file creation in site-packages directories

detective.name: Lifecycle script content analysis
detective.description: SCA tools that flag packages with suspicious install scripts

detective.name: Network monitoring during package installation
detective.description: Detect unexpected outbound connections during npm/pip install

detective.name: Process monitoring during installation
detective.description: EDR/runtime agent monitoring for child processes spawned by package managers

detective.name: File integrity monitoring for .pth files
detective.description: Alert on .pth file creation or modification in Python environments

data.customLabel: cook.pth + sitecustomize.py run on every Python interpreter start
data.evidence: litellm-1.107.0.data/purelib/{cook.pth,cook.py,sitecustomize.py}; sdist pyproject.toml adds data = "cook". Stealer encrypts (AES-256 + RSA-4096) and POSTs to www.litellm.dev/healthcheck; hourly loader execs code from domain in dead-drop file [Verified + Reporter]

data.name: Runner Executing Malicious Package
data.description: Malicious package executes on CI/CD runner
risks: Using untrusted SW packages on runners
data.customLabel: Runners installing litellm 1.107.0 / pulling :latest execute payload
data.evidence: Compromised CI runners among the sources of stolen AWS instance-role credentials [Wiz]

data.name: Secret Exfiltration from Workflow
data.description: Attacker extracts secrets from CI/CD workflow execution
data.customLabel: Runner env, cloud, AI-tool credentials exfiltrated to litellm.dev
data.evidence: Stealer collects developer, cloud and AI-tool credentials plus /proc/*/environ and exfiltrates encrypted [Reporter]

data.name: Steal Secrets from Production Environment
data.description: Attacker accesses production secrets store and exfiltrates customer secrets, tokens, and credentials
risks: Encryption keys accessible in process memory
Lack of hardware security module (HSM) for key storage
Centralized storage of all customer secrets
No data loss prevention (DLP) on production systems

protective.name: Store encryption keys in HSM (Hardware Security Module)

data.customLabel: Proxy DB dump: LiteLLM_CredentialsTable, LiteLLM_ProxyModelTable
data.evidence: If DATABASE_URL is set, payload dumps LiteLLM proxy credential and model tables (upstream LLM provider keys) [Reporter]

data.name: Cloud Metadata Service Exploitation
data.description: Attacker accesses cloud metadata service to steal additional credentials
data.customLabel: AWS instance-role credentials from K8s nodes
data.evidence: Wiz observed stolen AWS instance-role credentials from compromised CI runners and Kubernetes nodes [Wiz; IMDS retrieval inferred]

data.name: Cloud Service Lateral Movement
data.description: Attacker uses compromised cloud credentials to access other cloud services
data.customLabel: sts:GetCallerIdentity then Bedrock model listing (16:20-17:01Z)
data.evidence: Credential abuse began ~4.5h after exfiltration, consistent with LLMjacking [Wiz]

data.label: Secondary Supply Chain Attack
data.customLabel: Stolen CI/registry secrets from every litellm installer

data.label: Future Breach
data.customLabel: LLMjacking via stolen cloud credentials; hourly RCE loader

data.label: Endpoint/IDE
data.customLabel: Developer workstations

data.name: Malicious Execution on Endpoint
data.description: Attacker executes malicious code on developer workstation
risks: Using untrusted software packages on endpoints

protective.name: Automated maintainer reputation and hygiene checks

data.customLabel: pip install litellm: cook.pth runs on every Python start
data.evidence: Unpinned installs of 1.107.0 (PyPI 11:39-13:23Z) drop cook.pth/sitecustomize.py into site-packages; executes on any interpreter start, not just import of litellm. IOC: /tmp/.pc_once_* [Verified + LiteLLM post-mortem]

data.name: Harvest Local Secrets / Credentials from Endpoint
data.description: Attacker extracts credentials stored on developer machine
data.customLabel: Developer, cloud and AI-tool credentials harvested
data.evidence: Stealer targets developer, cloud and AI-tool credentials plus /proc/*/environ; AES-256 + RSA-4096 encrypted POST to www.litellm.dev/healthcheck. Endpoint victims inferred from payload targeting; Wiz-observed abuse came from CI runners and K8s nodes [Reporter + Inference]

data.name: Legitimate Service Abuse for C2
data.description: Attacker uses legitimate cloud services (Google Calendar, Pastebin, social media, cloud storage) as command and control channels to evade detection
risks: Legitimate services not monitored for C2 abuse
No content inspection of legitimate service traffic
Encoded payloads in legitimate service data

protective.name: Deep content inspection of legitimate service traffic

detective.name: Behavioral analysis for unusual service usage patterns

data.customLabel: Hourly loader reads C2 domain from GitHub dead drop
data.evidence: Loader fetches domain.txt from letters9813/pythonclient-test (GitHub) every hour and exec()s code from it; staged dormant (empty) since 10-20. IOC: /tmp/remote_code_loader.lock [Verified + Reporter]
